pages.title: Help & known issues
pages.intro: If something doesn't work, the fix is usually here. If nothing helps: under System → Health → Incidents, “Bug report” opens a prefilled report – without paths, names or secrets, you send it yourself.

tabsDetail.label: Windows blocks Hostwerk (Smart App Control)
tipTexts: On Windows 11, Smart App Control can block programs without a known signature. This affects the installer (Hostwerk-Setup-….exe), not Hostwerk itself.
Use the ZIP version, extract it e.g. to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Hostwerk and start Hostwerk.exe. On first start Hostwerk creates the shortcuts and the entry under “Apps”.
Hostwerk.exe is the unmodified, official Electron runtime. That's why Task Manager shows “Electron” – this is not an error.

Programs Hostwerk downloads (e.g. new Apache or PHP builds) are checked after the download. If Windows blocks one, Hostwerk tells you and suggests an alternative (nginx and Caddy have always worked so far).

tabsDetail.label: Port in use
tipTexts: A service doesn't start because “port 80” (or 3306, 25565 …) is already in use.
System → Health → Ports & services shows which program holds the port. If it's an old Hostwerk service, Hostwerk frees it with one click.
If it's another program (Skype, IIS, a second XAMPP, your own MariaDB …), simply set a different port for the service – or quit the other program.
New databases pick a free port on their own.

tabsDetail.label: Virus scanners
tipTexts: Virus scanners check every file a web server or database touches. That slows Hostwerk down, and sometimes a program (e.g. php.exe or mysqld.exe) is moved to quarantine.
Add the Hostwerk folder (default: %USERPROFILE%\Hostwerk) to your scanner's exclusions.
If a program suddenly goes missing, Hostwerk downloads it again on the next start (“self-healing”).

tabsDetail.label: WSL and Docker
tipTexts: On Windows, Docker apps and some game servers run in Hostwerk's own WSL environment (“hostwerk-docker”) – you don't need Docker Desktop.
Requirement: virtualization enabled in BIOS/UEFI and the Windows feature WSL. Hostwerk sets up WSL when needed; Windows asks for administrator rights and usually wants one restart.
“Timeout” doesn't mean “off”: the first start of a WSL environment sometimes takes Windows more than a minute. Just try again.
If Docker Desktop is already running, Hostwerk can use its engine.

tabsDetail.label: Proxy
tipTexts: Hostwerk doesn't use proxy settings yet. Behind a company proxy that blocks direct connections, downloads (PHP, databases, extensions, updates) fail.
Everything that works without the internet keeps running. With Settings → Privacy → Offline mode Hostwerk doesn't even try to connect.
An existing XAMPP installation can be taken over (Web servers → Import) without any download.

tabsDetail.label: Update stuck or doesn't start
tipTexts: Downloads resume after an interruption. If an update stands still for long, use Settings → App updates → Check for updates.
If a new version doesn't start, Hostwerk uses the previous one on the next start and skips the broken one.
Don't like a new version: Settings → App updates → Back to the previous version.
If Hostwerk runs as a system service, Live → Service shows “Update service” after an app update.

tabsDetail.label: System requirements
tipTexts: Windows: Windows 10 (22H2 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit (x64). ARM devices are not supported.
Linux: x64, glibc-based: Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, Debian 12, Fedora 40 or newer (AppImage or .deb).
Memory: 4 GB is enough for a web server and a database, 8 GB or more for Minecraft, Docker or the local AI helper.
Disk space: about 500 MB for Hostwerk, plus each service (PHP ~100 MB, a database ~300 MB, a Minecraft server 0.5–5 GB).

Administrator rights: Not needed to install or use Hostwerk. Windows only asks for: system service, firewall rules, setting up WSL/Docker. On Linux also for ports below 1024 and trusting the local certificate authority.

tabsDetail.label: Known issues in 2.x
tipTexts: Task Manager shows Hostwerk as “Electron” (see Smart App Control) – on purpose, so Windows doesn't block Hostwerk.
No downloads behind a proxy (see Proxy).
On Linux without a tray (plain GNOME), closing the window minimizes Hostwerk instead of hiding it.
Apache/PHP builds can occasionally be blocked by Smart App Control – nginx and Caddy are the fallback.

tabsDetail.label: Removing Hostwerk
tipTexts: Settings → Advanced → Remove Hostwerk cleans up everything Hostwerk registered in the system and asks whether your data should stay. If you uninstall through Windows (“Apps”), Hostwerk also removes its traces (autostart, certificates, system service, firewall rules) and keeps your data – a new installation finds it again.

tipTexts: How it works Install Hostwerk on the other machine (Windows or Linux; a rented server works with “Own server with one click”), switch on remote access there and enter the pairing code here. Then switch between the devices in the machine bar at the top – services, files, terminal and AI then run on the chosen machine. Linux servers in a data centre · Windows or Linux PCs at home · Phone: under Go live → Remote access

Rented server (e.g. at Hetzner, Netcup, IONOS) or a home server with Ubuntu, Debian or Fedora: Hostwerk sets itself up there – Node.js, Hostwerk without a window as a service, remote access with two-factor, firewall – and then shows up here as a machine. Your SSH sign-in is only used for the setup and never stored.
Another Hostwerk PC can then operate this machine – through remote access (HTTPS) with its own key that you can revoke at any time. The key is shown only once.

tabsDetail.label: Self-maintenance
tipTexts: What does “maintenance-free” mean? Hostwerk keeps itself and your services up to date: updates with a trial run and a way back, renewals, cleanup, restarts after crashes. Here you see per area whether that already runs on its own – clicking ⓘ explains exactly what happens and what is left for you.

Hostwerk itself Hostwerk checks daily for new versions, downloads them in the background and swaps them on the next start. If the new version doesn’t start cleanly, the previous one keeps running automatically. What you can do: Nothing – unless you want to skip versions (Settings → Updates).

PHP (patch versions) Every 6 hours Hostwerk looks for security updates within your PHP series (e.g. 8.3.x). The new version is installed next to the old one, tested with a trial run and only then activated. If the test fails, the old one stays. What you can do: You decide on bigger jumps (8.3 → 8.4) yourself – Hostwerk only suggests them.

Databases (patch versions) Like PHP: patch versions of MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL are checked, installed with a trial run and rolled back on errors. What you can do: You switch major versions yourself in the database area.
Web servers (patch versions) Apache, nginx and Caddy get security updates within their series – with a trial run; the old version stays as a way back. What you can do: Nothing.
Geyser/Floodgate Geyser and Floodgate (Bedrock players) are updated and tested automatically. What you can do: Nothing.
Certificates (Let’s Encrypt, local CA) HTTPS certificates (Let’s Encrypt and Hostwerk’s local certificate authority) are renewed in time. What you can do: Nothing – Hostwerk reports any error.

AI programs and models Ollama, image models, speech recognition and voices are updated with a trial run; the model catalogs arrive online daily. What you can do: If AI is turned off, there is nothing to do here.
Runtime (Node/Electron) Node.js and Electron, which Hostwerk runs on, are swapped with the app update – after a self-test. What you can do: Nothing.
Restore test The latest backup is regularly restored into a throwaway environment and checked. That way a broken backup is noticed before you need it. What you can do: Nothing.
Cleanup (leftovers, cache, trash) Hostwerk cleans up installation leftovers and old downloads daily; the trash is emptied after 30 days. What you can do: Nothing.

Self-healing (restart services) If a service crashes or stops responding, Hostwerk restarts it (with a pause so it doesn’t restart endlessly). What you can do: Nothing – incidents are listed under System → Incidents.
